name: ACT New Zealand
slogan: Campaigns on smaller government, lower tax and individual choice.

details.overview: ACT is a right-wing political party that emphasises individual freedom, personal responsibility, equal legal rights, private enterprise, economic growth and a smaller, more efficient government. ACT argues that government should focus on essential services while giving individuals and businesses greater freedom to make their own decisions.
details.currentStatus: The party is led by David Seymour, who is also Deputy Prime Minister.

policyAreas.title: Economy & taxation
policyAreas.text: Reduce government spending, regulation and bureaucracy, promote private investment and productivity, and support lower taxes where financially sustainable. ACT argues that economic growth and higher productivity are the primary ways to improve incomes and living standards.

policyAreas.title: Government
policyAreas.text: Reduce the size and complexity of government, with fewer departments and clearer ministerial accountability. ACT argues that government should provide better services while costing taxpayers less.

policyAreas.title: Law & order
policyAreas.text: Support tougher consequences for serious and repeat offending, stronger protections for victims and measures targeting gangs and criminal behaviour. ACT supports the restoration of Three Strikes legislation and a more enforcement-focused approach to crime.

policyAreas.title: Health
policyAreas.text: Focus government health spending on frontline services, improving access and reducing waiting times, while emphasising efficiency and measurable outcomes. ACT has also supported faster approval and funding of medicines.

policyAreas.title: Education
policyAreas.text: Emphasise literacy, numeracy, school attendance, academic achievement and greater choice in education. ACT supports charter schools and stronger accountability for educational outcomes.

policyAreas.title: Housing & infrastructure
policyAreas.text: Reduce planning and regulatory barriers to building, strengthen property rights and encourage councils to enable more housing and infrastructure development.

policyAreas.title: Workers & employment
policyAreas.text: Support employment, flexibility and economic growth while seeking to reduce what ACT considers unnecessary employment regulation and compliance costs for businesses.

policyAreas.title: Welfare
policyAreas.text: Place greater emphasis on moving people who can work from benefits into employment, with stronger obligations and time limits intended to reduce long-term welfare dependency.

policyAreas.title: Agriculture & rural New Zealand
policyAreas.text: Reduce regulatory burdens on farmers, support primary-sector productivity and oppose environmental rules that ACT considers unnecessarily restrictive. ACT has supported reducing methane-reduction requirements and expanding access to oil and gas exploration.

policyAreas.title: Environment & climate
policyAreas.text: Support environmental protection while placing greater emphasis on economic impacts, technological solutions and property rights. ACT has opposed what it considers overly costly climate regulations on agriculture and business.

policyAreas.title: Equal rights & Treaty policy
policyAreas.text: Emphasise equal legal rights for all New Zealand citizens regardless of ethnicity, gender or other characteristics. ACT opposes what it describes as race-based distinctions in government and has advocated redefining the legal interpretation of Treaty principles.

policyAreas.title: Immigration
policyAreas.text: Support immigration that fills genuine skills shortages and contributes economically, while proposing tighter requirements around skills, criminal offending, welfare eligibility and integration. ACT's current policy includes deportation provisions for certain serious offenders and a five-year stand-down from some benefits for residence-class migrants.

policyAreas.title: Firearms
policyAreas.text: Support firearm ownership for legitimate users while seeking stronger enforcement against criminal use and reforms to firearms regulation.

policyAreas.title: Business & regulation
policyAreas.text: Reduce red tape and regulatory requirements that ACT believes discourage investment, entrepreneurship and development. A major focus is expanding individual and property rights while limiting unnecessary government intervention.

details.position: ACT is generally positioned on the right, particularly on economic policy and the role of government. It places greater emphasis than National on individual freedom, private enterprise, personal responsibility, property rights and reducing government intervention. On some social issues, ACT also takes a strongly libertarian position, emphasising freedom of speech and equal legal rights.
details.simpleTerms: ACT's approach is broadly pro-freedom, pro-business and focused on personal responsibility, with a preference for a smaller, more efficient government, lower regulatory burdens and stronger property and individual rights.
details.caveat: This describes ACT's stated political position and current policies — it isn't an assessment of whether those policies would work or whether ACT's claims about its record are correct. Claims made by ACT about savings, crime, economic performance or the effects of its policies should be independently assessed rather than treated as established facts.

name: Green Party
slogan: Campaigns on climate action and social and environmental policy.

details.overview: The Green Party is a left-wing political party that emphasises environmental protection, climate action, social and economic equality, strong public services, workers' rights and the principles of Te Tiriti o Waitangi. Its political philosophy combines environmentalism with social justice and a greater role for government in addressing inequality and providing essential services.
details.currentStatus: The party's current campaign slogan is "For All of Us."

policyAreas.title: Economy & taxation
policyAreas.text: Support a more progressive tax system in which higher-income and high-wealth individuals contribute more, with additional government investment directed towards public services, housing, infrastructure and reducing poverty.

policyAreas.title: Climate & environment
policyAreas.text: Make rapid reductions in greenhouse-gas emissions, phase down fossil-fuel use, expand renewable energy and protect native ecosystems, waterways and biodiversity. The Greens are proposing a national electrification plan covering homes, transport and industry.

policyAreas.title: Health
policyAreas.text: Increase public investment in healthcare and improve access to timely, affordable services, including greater support for mental-health services and the health workforce.

policyAreas.title: Housing
policyAreas.text: Treat access to a warm, safe and affordable home as a basic need. Policies focus on increasing public and affordable housing, improving housing quality and addressing housing costs.

policyAreas.title: Workers & employment
policyAreas.text: Support higher incomes, stronger employment protections, collective bargaining and policies intended to improve workers' living standards.

policyAreas.title: Education
policyAreas.text: Support well-funded public education from early childhood through tertiary education, with an emphasis on accessibility, inclusion and reducing financial barriers to study.

policyAreas.title: Cost of living
policyAreas.text: Reduce household costs through measures involving housing, public transport, electricity and essential services. The Greens' current priorities specifically include making housing, transport, groceries and power bills more affordable.

policyAreas.title: Agriculture & land use
policyAreas.text: Promote more sustainable farming and forestry practices, protect waterways and soils, and support a food and fibre sector that reduces environmental impacts while maintaining rural employment.

policyAreas.title: Law & justice
policyAreas.text: Focus more strongly on preventing crime and addressing its underlying causes, alongside rehabilitation and reform of the justice system. The Greens generally favour a less punitive approach than National or ACT.

policyAreas.title: Māori & Te Tiriti
policyAreas.text: Support a stronger role for Te Tiriti o Waitangi in government and public decision-making, including greater recognition of Māori self-determination and the rights of iwi and hapū.

policyAreas.title: Drug policy
policyAreas.text: Support a health-based approach to drug use and drug-law reform, placing greater emphasis on harm reduction and treatment rather than criminal punishment.

policyAreas.title: Foreign affairs & defence
policyAreas.text: Promote an independent New Zealand foreign policy, international cooperation, human rights, peace and climate action, with opposition to greater military alignment where the Greens believe it compromises New Zealand's independence.

policyAreas.title: Social policy
policyAreas.text: Place strong emphasis on reducing poverty and inequality and improving outcomes for children, disabled people, women, rainbow communities and other groups experiencing disadvantage.

policyAreas.title: Business & industry
policyAreas.text: Support small and local businesses and sustainable industries, while favouring stronger regulation of large corporations where the Greens believe corporate power or environmental impacts are harming the public interest.

details.position: The Greens are generally positioned on the left, with a combination of environmentalism, social democracy, progressive social policy and stronger government intervention in the economy. Compared with Labour, the Greens generally advocate more aggressive climate action, greater redistribution of wealth, stronger environmental regulation and a larger expansion of public services.
details.simpleTerms: The Greens' approach is broadly pro-environment, pro-public services and focused on reducing inequality, with government playing a significant role in redistributing wealth, providing essential services, addressing climate change and protecting the environment.
details.caveat: This describes the Green Party's stated political position and current policies — it isn't an assessment of whether those policies would work or whether previous Green policies have succeeded. Claims made by the Greens about the economy, climate, poverty or government performance should be independently assessed rather than treated as established facts.

name: Labour Party
slogan: Campaigns on jobs, health and housing from a centre-left platform.

details.overview: Labour is a centre-left political party that emphasises strong public services, workers' rights, affordable housing, reducing inequality and government investment in health, education and infrastructure. Its current policy priorities are broadly centred on jobs, health and homes.
details.currentStatus: Labour is currently in Opposition, led by Chris Hipkins.

policyAreas.title: Economy & taxation
policyAreas.text: Support an economy focused on good jobs, decent wages, investment and productivity. Labour also proposes using government investment to support New Zealand businesses and infrastructure.

policyAreas.title: Health
policyAreas.text: Increase access to publicly funded healthcare. Current policies include three free GP visits per year for everyone, removing the $5 prescription charge, and expanding access to other health services.

policyAreas.title: Education
policyAreas.text: Support accessible public education, improve educational outcomes and invest in schools, teachers and student support.

policyAreas.title: Housing
policyAreas.text: Increase the supply of affordable homes, support home ownership and strengthen public and affordable housing provision.

policyAreas.title: Workers & employment
policyAreas.text: Emphasise employment standards, fair pay, job security and workers' rights, while supporting apprenticeships and skills development.

policyAreas.title: Infrastructure & transport
policyAreas.text: Increase investment in infrastructure and make public transport more affordable. Labour's current policy includes a $20 weekly public-transport fare cap in Auckland, Wellington and Christchurch and $10 elsewhere.

policyAreas.title: Business & industry
policyAreas.text: Establish a New Zealand Future Fund to invest in infrastructure and innovative New Zealand businesses, alongside policies aimed at supporting domestic industry and investment.

policyAreas.title: Environment & climate
policyAreas.text: Support greater investment in renewable energy and emissions reduction. Labour's current SolarSaver policy would provide government-backed finance to reduce the upfront cost of installing solar power.

policyAreas.title: Social policy
policyAreas.text: Focus on reducing poverty and inequality and providing support for families, children and people experiencing hardship.

policyAreas.title: Treaty & Māori policy
policyAreas.text: Labour supports the principles of Te Tiriti o Waitangi and opposes policies it considers to weaken Māori rights or the Treaty relationship.

details.position: Labour is generally positioned on the centre-left, favouring a larger role for government in providing public services, supporting workers and addressing inequality. It generally places greater emphasis than National on government investment, social programmes, employment protections and universal access to public services.
details.simpleTerms: Labour's approach is broadly pro-public services, pro-worker and focused on reducing inequality, with government playing a significant role in healthcare, education, housing, infrastructure and economic development.
details.caveat: This describes Labour's stated political position and current policies — it isn't an assessment of whether those policies have succeeded. Claims made by Labour about the economy, government performance or the effects of its policies should be independently assessed rather than treated as established facts.

name: National Party
slogan: Campaigns on economic management from a centre-right platform.

details.overview: National is a centre-right political party that emphasises economic growth, lower taxes, individual responsibility, private enterprise, public-service performance and law and order. Its stated values include ambition, success, rewarding hard work and equal opportunity.
details.currentStatus: National currently leads the New Zealand Government under Prime Minister Christopher Luxon. Its current political programme is centred on "fixing the basics and building the future."

policyAreas.title: Economy & taxation
policyAreas.text: Promote economic growth, productivity, investment and exports; maintain relatively low taxes; reduce government spending and debt.

policyAreas.title: Infrastructure
policyAreas.text: Increase investment in roads, housing-enabling infrastructure, schools, hospitals and other major projects, alongside resource-management reform intended to make development easier.

policyAreas.title: Law & order
policyAreas.text: Tougher penalties for serious offending, stronger action against gangs, additional police powers and greater police visibility.

policyAreas.title: Health
policyAreas.text: Increase access to healthcare, reduce waiting times, expand medicines and surgical capacity, and improve primary and after-hours care.

policyAreas.title: Education
policyAreas.text: Greater emphasis on reading, writing and mathematics, classroom resources and measurable educational achievement. National is also replacing NCEA with a new national qualification framework.

policyAreas.title: Housing
policyAreas.text: Increase housing supply through planning and resource-management reform, infrastructure investment and changes intended to make development easier.

policyAreas.title: Agriculture & business
policyAreas.text: Support the primary sector, exports, investment and business growth, with an emphasis on reducing regulatory barriers.

policyAreas.title: Foreign affairs & defence
policyAreas.text: Strengthen New Zealand's defence capability and international partnerships, particularly interoperability with Australia. National has stated that it intends to increase defence spending substantially if re-elected.

policyAreas.title: Environment & climate
policyAreas.text: Supports emissions reduction while placing greater emphasis on economic impacts, technological solutions and maintaining productive industries.

details.position: National is generally positioned on the centre-right, economically favouring lower taxation, private enterprise and restrained government spending, while supporting government provision of core services such as health, education, infrastructure and policing.
details.simpleTerms: National's approach is broadly pro-business, pro-growth and fiscally conservative, combined with a strong emphasis on public-service performance, infrastructure development, education standards and tougher law-and-order policies.
details.caveat: This describes National's stated political position and policies — it isn't an assessment of whether those policies have succeeded. Where National makes claims about its record (such as reductions in crime or improvements in the economy), those should be independently assessed rather than treated as established facts.

name: New Zealand First
slogan: Campaigns on national identity and a 'New Zealand first' platform.

details.overview: New Zealand First is a nationalist and populist political party that emphasises New Zealand sovereignty, equal citizenship, tighter immigration controls, stronger law and order, support for seniors and regional development. The party describes itself as pragmatic and focused on putting the interests of New Zealand and New Zealanders first.
details.currentStatus: It was founded in 1993 and is led by Winston Peters.

policyAreas.title: Economy & taxation
policyAreas.text: Support economic growth, export development and domestic industry, while maintaining a long-term objective of lower and simpler taxation. NZ First also favours government support for strategically important industries and infrastructure.

policyAreas.title: Cost of living
policyAreas.text: Target high grocery and power prices through stronger competition and regulation. Current policies include breaking up the supermarket duopoly and separating electricity generation and retail businesses.

policyAreas.title: Immigration
policyAreas.text: Support immigration where it provides skills and economic benefits, while placing greater emphasis on training and employing New Zealanders. NZ First currently proposes restricting voting rights to New Zealand citizens.

policyAreas.title: Law & order
policyAreas.text: Support tougher action against crime, stronger policing and measures targeting organised crime and gangs. The party's current priorities include additional frontline policing and stronger border security.

policyAreas.title: Health
policyAreas.text: Support a strong public health system and investment in healthcare services. Current government priorities supported by NZ First include maternity services and frontline health provision.

policyAreas.title: Education
policyAreas.text: Treat education as a long-term investment, with emphasis on improving skills, employment prospects and vocational training. Current policies include expanding Trades Academy places and Youth Guarantee opportunities.

policyAreas.title: Housing & infrastructure
policyAreas.text: Support increased infrastructure investment and development, particularly where it strengthens regional economies and national resilience.

policyAreas.title: Agriculture & regional development
policyAreas.text: Support the primary sector and greater value-added processing in New Zealand. Current policies include returning a share of mining royalties to the regions and encouraging domestic dairy manufacturing.

policyAreas.title: Energy & resources
policyAreas.text: Support greater domestic energy security and development of New Zealand's natural resources. Current proposals include additional strategic fuel reserves and investment in identifying and developing domestic energy resources.

policyAreas.title: Seniors
policyAreas.text: Strongly support superannuation and services for older New Zealanders. Current policies include modernising the SuperGold Card and expanding support for seniors.

policyAreas.title: Māori & Treaty policy
policyAreas.text: Emphasise equal citizenship and oppose what NZ First describes as race-based government policies and separatism. The party supports a referendum on the future of the Māori electorates and has proposed changes to the role of Treaty principles in government.

policyAreas.title: Democracy & sovereignty
policyAreas.text: Place strong emphasis on New Zealand's constitutional independence and national decision-making. Policies include greater scrutiny of international organisations and a proposed referendum on a four-year parliamentary term.

policyAreas.title: Environment
policyAreas.text: Support environmental protection while emphasising economic development, domestic resource security and what the party describes as pragmatic environmental policy.

policyAreas.title: Business & industry
policyAreas.text: Support New Zealand-owned businesses and strategic domestic industries. Current policies include proposals for a New Zealand-owned bank, stronger domestic dairy processing and greater regional control over resource revenues.

policyAreas.title: Defence & foreign affairs
policyAreas.text: Emphasise national sovereignty, New Zealand's independence in foreign policy and maintaining strong relationships within the region.

details.position: New Zealand First is generally positioned around the centre to centre-right, although it combines economic and social policies that don't fit neatly into a conventional left-right classification. It is particularly distinctive on national sovereignty, immigration, Treaty/Māori policy, regional development and opposition to what it considers excessive government bureaucracy or political correctness. Its economic approach can be interventionist where it believes strategic industries or consumers need government protection.
details.simpleTerms: New Zealand First's approach is broadly pro-national sovereignty, pro-New Zealand ownership and focused on immigration control, law and order, regional development and protecting the interests of New Zealand citizens, while taking a pragmatic approach to economic policy rather than consistently following either free-market or socialist principles.
details.caveat: This describes New Zealand First's stated political position and current policies — it isn't an assessment of whether those policies would work or whether the party's claims about government performance are correct. New Zealand First's current policy programme is evolving as the 2026 election campaign develops, so individual policies should be checked against the party's latest announcements.

name: Te Pāti Māori
slogan: Campaigns on Māori rights, Te Tiriti and indigenous-led policy.

details.overview: Te Pāti Māori is an Indigenous Māori political party that focuses on Māori self-determination, tino rangatiratanga, Te Tiriti o Waitangi, social and economic equality, environmental protection and Māori-led public services. The party advocates for Māori interests while describing its vision as an Aotearoa in which Tangata Whenua, Tangata Moana and Tangata Tiriti can thrive together.
details.currentStatus: The party is co-led by Debbie Ngarewa-Packer and Rawiri Waititi.

policyAreas.title: Economy & taxation
policyAreas.text: Support greater redistribution of wealth and resources, with stronger government investment aimed at reducing poverty and inequality. The party favours policies that increase economic security for low- and middle-income households and Māori communities.

policyAreas.title: Housing
policyAreas.text: Increase public and affordable housing, expand Māori housing and papakāinga development, and strengthen protections for renters. Current proposals include building 2,000 papakāinga homes, increasing public-housing investment and taxing property investors.

policyAreas.title: Health
policyAreas.text: Support greater Māori decision-making and Māori-led delivery of health services, with a focus on reducing health inequities and improving access to culturally appropriate healthcare.

policyAreas.title: Education
policyAreas.text: Support Māori-led education, strengthening te reo Māori and mātauranga Māori, and increasing Māori influence over education policy and institutions.

policyAreas.title: Workers & employment
policyAreas.text: Support higher living standards, stronger worker protections and policies aimed at reducing poverty and economic inequality.

policyAreas.title: Justice & crime
policyAreas.text: Move away from mass imprisonment and toward prevention, rehabilitation and community-led justice. Te Pāti Māori supports repealing Three Strikes and ultimately creating a society where prisons are no longer needed.

policyAreas.title: Māori & Te Tiriti
policyAreas.text: Place Te Tiriti o Waitangi, tino rangatiratanga and mana motuhake at the centre of government. The party supports constitutional change intended to give Māori greater authority over decisions affecting Māori communities.

policyAreas.title: Te reo Māori & culture
policyAreas.text: Strengthen and normalise te reo Māori throughout New Zealand, invest in language revitalisation and protect Māori cultural rights and expressions.

policyAreas.title: Environment & climate
policyAreas.text: Protect whenua, wai and biodiversity and pursue stronger climate action. The party supports Māori-led environmental decision-making and greater recognition of mātauranga Māori in climate policy.

policyAreas.title: Agriculture & food
policyAreas.text: Promote Māori control of food systems, regenerative Māori agriculture and greater access to land for food production. The party also supports protecting Māori food sovereignty and seed sovereignty.

policyAreas.title: Social policy
policyAreas.text: Focus strongly on reducing poverty, improving outcomes for whānau and children, and strengthening Māori community organisations and whānau-led services.

policyAreas.title: Child welfare
policyAreas.text: Reduce state intervention in Māori families and increase whānau authority over the care of Māori children. The party wants greater accountability for harm caused through state care and uplifts.

policyAreas.title: Drug policy
policyAreas.text: Support a health and harm-reduction approach to drug use rather than relying primarily on criminal penalties. Decriminalisation of drug use is part of the party's longer-term justice approach.

policyAreas.title: Democracy & constitutional reform
policyAreas.text: Seek greater recognition of Māori political authority and Te Tiriti-based constitutional arrangements. Te Pāti Māori also supports expanding democratic participation, including lowering the voting age to 16 and restoring voting rights for prisoners.

policyAreas.title: Foreign affairs
policyAreas.text: Support an independent foreign policy with a strong emphasis on Indigenous rights, self-determination and human rights. The party has also taken strong positions supporting Palestinian self-determination and opposing Israel's occupation and settlement policies.

details.position: Te Pāti Māori is generally positioned on the left, but its political identity is primarily centred on Māori self-determination and Indigenous rights rather than the conventional left-right spectrum. It generally advocates a larger role for government in redistribution, public services, housing and environmental protection, while seeking substantially greater Māori authority over decisions affecting Māori.
details.simpleTerms: Te Pāti Māori's approach is broadly pro-Māori self-determination, pro-Te Tiriti and focused on reducing inequality, with strong emphasis on Māori-led health, education, housing, justice and environmental policy.
details.caveat: This describes Te Pāti Māori's stated political position and current policies — it isn't an assessment of whether those policies would work or whether the party's claims about government performance are correct. Some of its proposals — particularly around constitutional transformation, Māori authority and the future of the justice system — represent significant changes from New Zealand's current arrangements and are therefore matters of political debate rather than established outcomes.

name: Animal Justice Party Aotearoa NZ
slogan: Campaigns on animal rights and welfare policy.

details.overview: The Animal Justice Party Aotearoa New Zealand (AJP) is a political party focused primarily on animal rights and welfare, environmental sustainability and creating a society that considers the interests of animals alongside those of people. The party argues that animals are sentient beings rather than commodities or resources and supports significant changes to the way animals are treated in agriculture, research, entertainment and society. Its broader policy platform also covers environmental, social and economic issues.
details.currentStatus: The party is currently campaigning for the 2026 general election under the message "Animals. Environment. People."

policyAreas.title: Animal rights & welfare
policyAreas.text: Give animals stronger legal protection and greater consideration in government decision-making. The party supports recognising animals as individuals with inherent value rather than primarily as resources for human use.

policyAreas.title: Agriculture
policyAreas.text: Move away from intensive animal agriculture and support a transition towards plant-based and more sustainable food production. The party opposes practices it considers harmful to animal welfare, including intensive winter grazing.

policyAreas.title: Fishing & hunting
policyAreas.text: Ban recreational fishing and fishing competitions, as well as recreational hunting and hunting competitions.

policyAreas.title: Animal experimentation
policyAreas.text: Ban harmful experimentation on animals and promote alternatives to animal-based research.

policyAreas.title: Animal entertainment
policyAreas.text: End the use of animals for entertainment and support affected workers and industries through a planned transition. Policies include opposition to horse racing and rodeo.

policyAreas.title: Animal breeding & products
policyAreas.text: End commercial breeding of companion animals and oppose the production of fur and leather.

policyAreas.title: Animal protection
policyAreas.text: Establish a Commissioner for Animals with legal authority and responsibility for monitoring animal welfare across different sectors.

policyAreas.title: Companion animals
policyAreas.text: Improve protections for pets, including support for pets being allowed on public transport and compassionate leave relating to the death or serious illness of companion animals.

policyAreas.title: Climate & environment
policyAreas.text: Pursue stronger action on climate change, protect ecosystems and biodiversity, reduce pollution and move towards an economy operating within environmental limits.

policyAreas.title: Plant-based economy
policyAreas.text: Support a long-term transition towards a more plant-based economy, linking animal welfare with environmental sustainability and human health.

policyAreas.title: Economy
policyAreas.text: Promote what the party describes as a sustainable economy that operates within planetary boundaries rather than prioritising economic growth regardless of environmental consequences.

policyAreas.title: Workers & just transition
policyAreas.text: Support workers and communities affected by changes to industries that rely on animal exploitation, with the party advocating a planned and compassionate transition rather than simply removing existing industries.

policyAreas.title: Māori & Te Tiriti
policyAreas.text: Embrace Te Tiriti o Waitangi and support its role in creating what the party describes as a compassionate, equitable and cooperative relationship between people, animals and the environment.

policyAreas.title: Social policy
policyAreas.text: Promote equality, inclusivity and non-discrimination, applying these principles across species as well as within human society.

policyAreas.title: Emergency planning
policyAreas.text: Support including animals in Civil Defence and disaster-response planning and providing dedicated funding for animal rescue organisations and emergency animal response.

policyAreas.title: Live animal exports
policyAreas.text: Oppose the export of live animals by sea and support maintaining New Zealand's prohibition on the trade.

details.position: The Animal Justice Party doesn't fit neatly into the traditional left-right political spectrum. Its defining political philosophy is animal rights, combined with environmentalism, sustainability, non-violence and social equality. On economic and environmental issues, many of its policies involve greater government regulation and intervention, particularly where animal welfare and environmental protection are concerned.
details.simpleTerms: The Animal Justice Party's approach is broadly pro-animal rights, pro-environment and focused on reducing harm to animals, with a long-term goal of moving New Zealand towards a more plant-based and sustainable economy. It advocates significant changes to agriculture, animal research, hunting, fishing, entertainment and other industries involving animals.
details.caveat: This describes the Animal Justice Party's stated political position and policies — it isn't an assessment of whether those policies would work or whether the party's claims about animal welfare, agriculture, climate or the economy are correct. Some of its proposals — particularly transitioning away from animal agriculture and banning recreational fishing, hunting and animal-based entertainment — would represent substantial changes to existing industries and practices.

name: Aotearoa Legalise Cannabis Party
slogan: Campaigns on cannabis law reform and drug policy.

details.overview: The Aotearoa Legalise Cannabis Party (ALCP) is a single-issue political party primarily focused on legalising and regulating cannabis in New Zealand. The party argues that cannabis prohibition causes unnecessary criminalisation and that a regulated legal market would allow cannabis to be controlled, taxed and subject to quality and safety standards.
details.currentStatus: The party has contested every general election since its formation in 1996 but has never won a seat in Parliament.

policyAreas.title: Cannabis legalisation
policyAreas.text: Legalise the possession, cultivation and use of cannabis by adults, with a regulated legal framework rather than criminal prohibition.

policyAreas.title: Cannabis regulation
policyAreas.text: Establish a regulated cannabis market covering production, distribution and sale, with controls intended to manage potential harms.

policyAreas.title: Medical cannabis
policyAreas.text: Expand access to cannabis for medicinal purposes and reduce barriers for people using cannabis for medical conditions.

policyAreas.title: Cannabis taxation
policyAreas.text: Tax the legal cannabis industry, with government revenue replacing some of the economic activity currently associated with the illegal market. The party argues that regulation could reduce criminal-market revenue while generating legitimate economic activity.

policyAreas.title: Cannabis convictions
policyAreas.text: Support removing or expunging criminal records for people convicted of offences relating to cannabis possession or use that would no longer be criminal under a legalised system. Its 2026 campaign material specifically advocates cannabis conviction expungement.

policyAreas.title: Hemp
policyAreas.text: Support wider cultivation and use of industrial hemp, including removing unnecessary licensing barriers and encouraging hemp-based products and industries.

policyAreas.title: Drug education
policyAreas.text: Support greater investment in drug education and research, with an emphasis on providing factual information about cannabis and other drugs rather than relying primarily on prohibition.

policyAreas.title: Police & justice
policyAreas.text: Reduce the criminal-justice resources devoted to cannabis possession and personal use and redirect the focus towards serious crime and drug-related harm.

policyAreas.title: Personal freedom
policyAreas.text: Emphasise individual autonomy and the right of adults to make decisions about cannabis use without unnecessary criminal penalties.

policyAreas.title: Economic development
policyAreas.text: Support development of a legitimate cannabis and hemp industry, including opportunities for agriculture, manufacturing, research and exports where legally and economically viable.

policyAreas.title: Human rights
policyAreas.text: Argue that cannabis prohibition can result in disproportionate policing and criminalisation and advocate greater protection of the rights of cannabis users.

details.position: The ALCP does not fit particularly neatly onto the traditional left-right spectrum. Its defining issue is cannabis legalisation and drug-law reform. On this issue it takes a substantially more liberal position than the major parties. Its broader policies have historically included themes of personal freedom, human rights, environmental sustainability and social justice.
details.simpleTerms: The ALCP's approach is broadly pro-cannabis legalisation, pro-regulation and focused on personal freedom, with the aim of replacing cannabis prohibition with a legal, regulated system covering adult use, medical access, cultivation, taxation and industry.
details.caveat: This describes the Aotearoa Legalise Cannabis Party's stated political position and policies — it isn't an assessment of whether legalisation would produce the claimed economic, health or criminal-justice outcomes. The party's current 2026 policy platform should be checked against its latest election material, as its publicly available policy information is less extensive and less frequently updated than that of the larger parliamentary parties.

name: Conservative Party NZ
slogan: Campaigns on socially conservative and family-values policy.

details.overview: The Conservative Party NZ is a socially and fiscally conservative political party that emphasises traditional family values, individual responsibility, freedom of speech, limited government, lower taxation, national sovereignty and stronger controls on immigration. The party was originally established as the Conservative Party in 2011, later becoming New Conservative, and is now registered as Conservative Party NZ.
details.currentStatus: It currently has no MPs in Parliament. The Electoral Commission currently lists the registered party as Conservative Party NZ, with Helen Houghton as its leader.

policyAreas.title: Economy & taxation
policyAreas.text: Support lower taxation, reduced government spending and a smaller public sector, with greater emphasis on individual responsibility and private enterprise.

policyAreas.title: Government
policyAreas.text: Reduce bureaucracy and the size of government, while increasing accountability and giving citizens a greater role in political decision-making.

policyAreas.title: Direct democracy
policyAreas.text: Strongly support binding citizens-initiated referendums. The party's current proposal would allow a referendum to become binding if it received at least a two-thirds majority with minimum voter participation.

policyAreas.title: Family & social policy
policyAreas.text: Place strong emphasis on traditional family structures, parental responsibility and protecting children from what the party considers inappropriate ideological influence.

policyAreas.title: Education
policyAreas.text: Support greater parental choice and oppose the teaching of what the party describes as "gender ideology" in schools. The party campaigned on this position during the 2023 election.

policyAreas.title: Law & justice
policyAreas.text: Support stronger consequences for serious offending while also emphasising rehabilitation and the rights of victims.

policyAreas.title: Free speech
policyAreas.text: Strongly support freedom of expression and oppose government restrictions that the party believes unnecessarily limit political or social debate.

policyAreas.title: Immigration
policyAreas.text: Support tighter immigration controls, with greater emphasis on immigration levels, skills, integration and the interests of existing New Zealand citizens. The party has recently focused particularly on the scale and effects of migration from India.

policyAreas.title: Māori & Te Tiriti
policyAreas.text: Emphasise equal citizenship and oppose policies that the party considers create different legal or political rights based on ethnicity. This places the party in opposition to some forms of Māori-specific representation and policy.

policyAreas.title: Environment
policyAreas.text: Support environmental protection while favouring approaches that the party considers economically practical and compatible with property rights, agriculture and economic development.

policyAreas.title: Agriculture & rural New Zealand
policyAreas.text: Support farmers and rural communities and generally favour reducing regulatory burdens that the party believes restrict agricultural production.

policyAreas.title: Energy & resources
policyAreas.text: Support greater development of New Zealand's domestic natural resources and energy resources where the party believes this would improve energy security and economic growth.

policyAreas.title: Health
policyAreas.text: Support a publicly funded healthcare system while favouring greater efficiency, individual choice and a role for private healthcare providers.

policyAreas.title: Housing
policyAreas.text: Support increasing housing supply and affordability through reducing regulatory barriers and encouraging private development.

policyAreas.title: Firearms
policyAreas.text: Historically supported greater firearm ownership rights and opposed some of the firearms restrictions introduced after the Christchurch mosque attacks, although the party's current policy position should be checked against its latest election platform.

policyAreas.title: Constitution & sovereignty
policyAreas.text: Support greater protection of individual rights, New Zealand's constitutional independence and democratic control by New Zealand citizens.

details.position: The Conservative Party NZ is generally positioned on the right, combining social conservatism with fiscally conservative economic policies. Compared with National, it generally takes a stronger position on traditional social values, immigration restriction, direct democracy and limiting government intervention in areas such as speech and individual behaviour. It is also generally more socially conservative than ACT.
details.simpleTerms: The Conservative Party NZ's approach is broadly pro-traditional values, pro-free speech and individual responsibility, with a preference for smaller government, lower taxes, tighter immigration controls and greater direct public influence over political decisions.
details.caveat: This describes the Conservative Party NZ's stated political position and policies — it isn't an assessment of whether those policies would work or whether the party's claims are correct. The party has changed its name, leadership and some policy positions over time, so older descriptions of the former New Conservative Party should not automatically be treated as its current 2026 platform.

name: NZ Outdoors & Freedom Party
slogan: Campaigns on outdoor access rights and personal freedoms.

details.overview: The NZ Outdoors & Freedom Party is a minor political party focused on individual freedom, outdoor recreation, environmental and conservation issues, personal choice, direct democracy and reducing government overreach. The party was originally founded as the New Zealand Outdoors Party and later adopted its current name.
details.currentStatus: Sue Grey is its leader. The party currently has no representation in Parliament. It became associated with the wider Freedoms NZ movement in 2023, alongside groups including Vision NZ, during the post-COVID period; Freedoms NZ subsequently disbanded in 2025, and the Outdoors & Freedom Party continues independently.

policyAreas.title: Individual freedom
policyAreas.text: Emphasise personal liberty, informed choice and limiting government powers where the party believes they unnecessarily restrict individual freedoms.

policyAreas.title: Direct democracy
policyAreas.text: Support greater use of referendums and mechanisms that give citizens more direct influence over government decisions.

policyAreas.title: Outdoor recreation
policyAreas.text: Promote access to New Zealand's outdoors, including hunting, fishing, camping and other recreational activities, while supporting responsible management of natural resources.

policyAreas.title: Agriculture
policyAreas.text: Support farmers and rural communities while advocating agricultural practices that the party considers environmentally sustainable.

policyAreas.title: Fisheries
policyAreas.text: Support recreational fishing rights and changes to fisheries management intended to protect access for recreational fishers and improve sustainability.

policyAreas.title: Cannabis
policyAreas.text: Support cannabis law reform and greater personal freedom around cannabis use, alongside regulation and harm-reduction measures.

policyAreas.title: Housing
policyAreas.text: Support policies intended to make housing more accessible and affordable, including changes to planning and regulation.

policyAreas.title: Education
policyAreas.text: Support greater choice, parental involvement and approaches to education that the party considers practical and evidence-based.

policyAreas.title: Health
policyAreas.text: Support accessible healthcare while emphasising personal choice, informed consent and individual autonomy in healthcare decisions.

policyAreas.title: ACC
policyAreas.text: Advocate changes to ACC and compensation arrangements, with a focus on individual rights and ensuring people receive appropriate support.

policyAreas.title: Seniors
policyAreas.text: Support stronger recognition and protection of the interests of older New Zealanders.

policyAreas.title: Environment & conservation
policyAreas.text: Support protection of New Zealand's natural environment while arguing that conservation policies should take account of recreational access, rural communities and local interests.

policyAreas.title: Media & free speech
policyAreas.text: Support greater media accountability and freedom of expression. A 2026 proposal would amend broadcasting legislation to strengthen requirements around media balance and accountability.

policyAreas.title: Digital rights
policyAreas.text: Support keeping New Zealand-developed digital intellectual property and infrastructure within New Zealand where possible. The party describes this as an "Open Source First" approach.

policyAreas.title: Animal welfare
policyAreas.text: Support animal welfare while balancing this against farming, hunting, fishing and other activities involving animals.

policyAreas.title: Government & regulation
policyAreas.text: Seek to reduce unnecessary regulation and government intervention, particularly where the party believes these restrict individual freedom, outdoor recreation or rural livelihoods.

details.position: The NZ Outdoors & Freedom Party does not fit neatly into the traditional left-right spectrum. It is generally associated with the freedom-oriented and populist right, particularly because of its emphasis on individual liberty, opposition to government overreach and support for personal choice. However, its environmental, conservation and outdoor-recreation policies don't always align neatly with conventional right-wing parties.
details.simpleTerms: The NZ Outdoors & Freedom Party's approach is broadly pro-individual freedom, pro-outdoors and focused on personal choice, direct democracy and limiting government overreach, while also placing significant emphasis on access to New Zealand's natural environment and rural interests.
details.caveat: This describes the party's stated political position and policies — it isn't an assessment of whether those policies would work or whether the party's claims are correct. The party has changed its name and political associations over time, so older descriptions of the former Outdoors Party or its 2023 association with Freedoms NZ should not automatically be treated as its current position.

name: Opportunities Party (TOP)
slogan: Campaigns on evidence-based policy and a universal basic income.

details.overview: The Opportunity Party (TOP) is a centrist political party that emphasises evidence-based policymaking, economic reform, housing affordability, environmental sustainability, political reform and improving opportunities for New Zealanders. The party was founded in 2016 and, following a rebrand and change of leadership, is contesting the 2026 general election under leader Qiulae Wong.
details.currentStatus: Its current programme focuses on fixing politics, building a new economy and restoring nature. The party has attracted substantially more attention during the 2026 campaign than in previous elections — a recent Taxpayers' Union–Curia poll put it at 6.1%, above the 5% MMP threshold, although this is only one poll and shouldn't be read as a prediction of the election result.

policyAreas.title: Economy & taxation
policyAreas.text: Reform the tax system to place greater emphasis on taxing wealth and land rather than productive activity. A central proposal is a land-value tax, intended to reduce property speculation and encourage more productive use of land.

policyAreas.title: Citizen's income
policyAreas.text: Replace existing welfare payments, including NZ Superannuation, with a means-tested Citizen's Income. Under the current proposal, people earning more than $350,000 would not receive it. The policy would be funded partly through a land-value tax and savings from replacing existing welfare programmes.

policyAreas.title: Housing
policyAreas.text: Address housing affordability by changing taxation and incentives around land, with the land-value tax intended to discourage speculative holding of land and encourage development.

policyAreas.title: Environment & oceans
policyAreas.text: Strengthen environmental protection, with current priorities including healthier oceans and a proposed ban on bottom trawling.

policyAreas.title: Energy
policyAreas.text: Support significantly greater investment in renewable and abundant energy, with the aim of providing cheaper energy and supporting economic development.

policyAreas.title: Economic productivity
policyAreas.text: Focus on improving New Zealand's productivity and developing a higher-value economy rather than relying heavily on low-productivity industries. The party describes this as a "Breakthrough Economy."

policyAreas.title: Infrastructure & transport
policyAreas.text: Support long-term infrastructure planning, greater investment in infrastructure and electrification, alongside policies intended to improve public transport and reduce transport emissions.

policyAreas.title: Political reform
policyAreas.text: Introduce greater citizen participation in major decisions through a "Citizens' Voice", including citizens' assemblies on significant issues.

policyAreas.title: Government & politics
policyAreas.text: Seek changes intended to make government more transparent, accountable and evidence-based. The party's current programme includes "Clean Up Politics" as one of its major priorities.

policyAreas.title: Business & innovation
policyAreas.text: Encourage investment, innovation and higher-productivity businesses, while using economic policy to shift investment towards activities that generate greater long-term value.

policyAreas.title: Agriculture
policyAreas.text: Support a transition towards more sustainable and productive land use while recognising the importance of agriculture to the New Zealand economy.

policyAreas.title: Social policy
policyAreas.text: Focus on improving economic opportunity and reducing structural disadvantages, particularly through changes to taxation, welfare and housing.

policyAreas.title: National unity
policyAreas.text: The party has made national unity one of its 2026 campaign themes, seeking to move political debate away from polarisation and towards shared national interests.

details.position: The Opportunity Party is generally positioned in the centre, although its policies don't fit neatly into traditional left-right categories. It combines market-oriented economic reform with significant government intervention through taxation, welfare reform and environmental regulation. Its emphasis on evidence-based policy, political reform and environmental sustainability also differentiates it from the major centre-right and centre-left parties.
details.simpleTerms: The Opportunity Party's approach is broadly centrist, evidence-focused and reform-oriented, with particular emphasis on housing affordability, tax reform, economic productivity, environmental protection, renewable energy and giving citizens a greater role in political decision-making.
details.caveat: This describes the Opportunity Party's stated political position and current policies — it isn't an assessment of whether those policies would work. Some of its proposals — particularly replacing NZ Superannuation and other welfare payments with a Citizen's Income and introducing a land-value tax — would represent significant changes to New Zealand's existing economic and welfare systems. The party's policy platform is also evolving during the 2026 election campaign, so its latest policy announcements should take precedence.

name: Vision New Zealand
slogan: Campaigns on faith-based community and family policy.

name: Women's Rights Party
slogan: Campaigns on sex-based rights for women and girls.

name: The Alliance
slogan: Campaigns on public ownership, workers' rights and Treaty partnership.

name: Build The Nation
slogan: Campaigns on a Northland-founded platform for regional New Zealand.
